item.title: Matrix nearness problems via Lie algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.28046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As examplified by the Eckart--Young theorem, a matrix nearness problem can be solve by only manipulating only singular values despite having geometrically complicated constraints. In this article, we answer the question of when a matrix nearness problem $D(A,X)$ or $D(X,A)$ can be solved by only manipulating the eigenvalues or singular values of $A$ via the notion of isotropic divergences. We show under an isotropic divergence, a matrix nearness problem with constraints respecting the Lie group symmetry can always be reduced to approximating the eigenvalues or singular values of $A$, providing a systematic way to construct the minimizers. We provide sufficient conditions of isotropy in the classes of Bregman, Jensen, and Calabi's diastasis and verify that a myriad of matrix divergences arising in applications are naturally isotropic, including the Frobenius, von Neumann, logdet, $S$-, quantum Jensen--Shannon, Bures--Wasserstein, quantum Hellinger, and quantum $q$-divergence, among others. This procedure opens the door to for us to construct solutions to a myriad of matrix nearness problems including constraints on rank, spectrum, condition number, trace, determinant, as well as other physically motivated constraints.
item.dc:creator: Rongbiao Thomas Wang

item.title: Critical exponents and spectral functions of totally nonnegative matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.28051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the ordinary critical exponent for total positivity. For every oscillatory matrix $A$ of order $n\ge2$, the power $A^t$ is totally positive for $t>n-2$, and this bound is optimal. More generally, if $\psi$ is real and operator monotone on $(0,\infty)$, then $A^\alpha e^{\psi(A)}$ is totally nonnegative for every nonsingular totally nonnegative matrix $A$ of order $n$ when $\alpha\ge n-2$. In this range, if $A$ is oscillatory, the matrix is totally positive when $\alpha>n-2$ or $\psi$ is nonconstant. If $A$ is totally positive and $n\ge4$, every minor of $A^\alpha e^{\psi(A)}$ is positive for $\alpha\ge n-3$ except possibly the $(1,n)$ and $(n,1)$ entries and the two far corners of order $n-1$. In particular, it is a P-matrix. The exponents $t$ for which $A^t$ is a P-matrix for every totally positive matrix $A$ of order $n$ form $\mathbb Z\cup\{t:|t|\ge n-3\}$ for $n\ge4$, and all of $\mathbb R$ for $n\le3$. For $1\le p<n$, the minors of $A^t$ whose row or column set consists of the first or last $p$ indices have sharp tail threshold $\max(p,n-p)-1$ as $A$ ranges over totally positive matrices of order $n$. For a fixed order $n\ge2$, a positive analytic function that preserves nonsingular totally nonnegative matrices maps every oscillatory matrix to a totally positive matrix if and only if it is not a positive multiple of $x^k$ for $k\in\{0,\ldots,n-2\}$.
item.dc:creator: Wei Xie

item.title: An order on the Leech lattice from a $\mathbb{Z}_3$-symmetric triple-octonion product
item.description: arXiv:2611.28058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Leech lattice $\Lambda$ admits the structure of an order in a 24-dimensional real algebra: the lattice is closed under a bilinear product on $\mathbb{R}^{24}$, assembled from nine octonion-multiplication blocks under cyclic $\mathbb{Z}_3$ permutation of three octonion factors. In Robert A. Wilson's sublattice description of $\Lambda$, closure turns on a transposition $\sigma$ of two imaginary basis units: $\sigma$ leaves the $E_8$ lattice $L$ invariant and is an octonion-algebra isomorphism, but moves Wilson's two sublattices of $L$. The proof reduces to four lemmas, three of which follow from the closure of one maximal order of integral octonions. More generally, for every linear map $g$ with $g(L) = L$, the triple product built from the $g$-twisted octonion product closes on $\Lambda$ exactly when Wilson's two sublattices are closed under that product. We determine the idempotents, the square-zero elements, and the automorphism group of the algebra, as well as the automorphism group of the order and the index of the span of its products. We discuss the construction in the context of related work. A historical appendix (1923--1946) traces $\sigma$ to Richard H. Bruck's repair of Johannes Kirmse's integral octonions. The research record of this human--AI collaboration is public.
item.dc:creator: Jens K\"oplinger

item.title: On Tensor Invertibility and Spectral Localization under the M-Product
item.description: arXiv:2611.28069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growth of multidimensional data demands rigorous multilinear algebraic frameworks. While M-product tensor transformations mimic matrix operations over a commutative ring of tubal scalars, the presence of zero-divisors has historically limited theoretical analysis. To overcome these limitations, in this paper, we introduce a novel tubal determinant to rigorously define tensor invertibility and resolve the zero-divisor effect (McCoy defect). We also prove a tubal rank-nullity theorem using projective submodules and formalize tubal spectral analysis, yielding a novel Gershgorin hypersphere theorem. In addition to this, we find the Frobenius perturbation bounds for the pseudoinverse. Supporting the theoretical algebraic results, some numerical examples and visual illustrations are also provided in this paper. Finally, the theoretical results are applied experimentally for numerical illustrations. These results are essential and form the backbone for the theoretical analysis of tensor-based algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Aneesh Panchal, Ratikanta Behera

item.title: Algebras Generated by Two Idempotent Matrices: Classification up to Isomorphism and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.28086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is a continuation of the earlier work by the author and Falguni Roy \cite{biswas2025comprehensive} on the algebra \(\operatorname{alg}(P,Q)\) generated by two idempotent matrices \(P,Q\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}\). A complete classification of these algebras up to algebra isomorphism is presented, without imposing any additional restrictions on the idempotents. As an application, group invertibility in \(\operatorname{alg}(P,Q)\) is employed to obtain an explicit solution to a particular system of linear equations.
item.dc:creator: Rounak Biswas

item.title: Leavitt path algebras, growth series, Thompson groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.28188v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider several problems related to the growth of Leavitt path algebras with respect to the natural length filtration. We define the generating function of the series of dimensions of the successive quotients of this filtration and show that it is a rational function with poles which are reciprocal of the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix, a fact which is related to recent results by Bock, Gil Canto, Mart\'in Barquero, Mart\'in Gonz\'alez, Ruiz Campos and Sebandal on algebraic entropy of Leavitt path algebras. We also consider the filtration induced in the topological full group of the Renault-Deaconu groupoid of the defining graph and study the growth of the associated series. In the particular case of Thompson's group $V$, we find double exponential upper and lower bounds for this growth. We also prove related results for the group $F$ and for some submonoids.
item.dc:creator: Conchita Mart\'inez-P\'erez, Sof\'ia Sir\'on

item.title: Associative operators and their iterated lifts: classification and cocycle identities
item.description: arXiv:2611.28273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The inverse problem of an inhomogeneous functional equation asks for which right-hand sides the equation is solvable. For the Cauchy equation and for the quadratic equation a necessary condition is a cocycle identity, and the two identities have a common form. We take this form as a definition. An operator from functions of one variable to functions of two variables can be lifted to functions of several variables, one argument at a time. We call it associative when its two iterated lifts from one variable to three coincide, that is, when every function in its image satisfies the corresponding cocycle identity. Composition with an associative binary operation is the model case. The Cauchy difference, the d'Alembert operator and the Jordan-von Neumann operator are associative as well. We prove that all iterated lifts of the same length of an associative operator coincide. Over abelian groups we classify, under suitable hypotheses, the associative integer combinations of translations, embeddings and the evaluation at the origin. For a composition operator the cocycle identity characterises the image over monoids and over bands. Over an arbitrary semigroup we reduce this question to the injectivity of a canonical map.
item.dc:creator: Dorian Popa, Mircea Dan Rus, Constantin-Cosmin Todea

item.title: Polynomial identities of the two-dimensional simple right-symmetric algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.28826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe a basis for the polynomial identities satisfied by the unique two-dimensional simple right-symmetric algebra $B$ over a field of characteristic zero. Modulo the right-symmetric identity, this basis consists of two irreducible identities of degree three. We construct linear bases for the multilinear components of the relatively free algebra of the variety $\mathcal V=\operatorname{var}(B)$ and determine their decompositions into Specht modules. Using the resulting $S_n$-module decompositions, we prove that the commutator subspace is right nilpotent in every proper subvariety of $\mathcal V$. Moreover, in any proper subvariety satisfying a nontrivial identity of degree $n\ge2$, the index of right nilpotence of the commutator subspace is at most $2n$.
item.dc:creator: Nurlan Ismailov, Ualbai Umirbaev

item.title: Finite conformal models and the Kac--van de Leur conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.29212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every simple Lie superalgebra containing the centerless Virasoro algebra, with diagonal $L_0$-action, uniformly bounded weight multiplicities, and support in finitely many cosets of $\Z$, is isomorphic, as a parity-graded Lie superalgebra, to a member of the Witt, special, contact, or Cheng--Kac families. Thus the amended Kac--van de Leur list is exhaustive. Every such algebra admits a finite ordinary conformal model and is a quotient by the full center of a twisted coefficient algebra of a finite simple conformal superalgebra. For Lie superalgebras containing the centerless Virasoro algebra, we also prove that linear commutator growth is equivalent to uniformly bounded weight spaces, provided the grading is diagonal and integral and each weight space is finite-dimensional.
item.dc:creator: Haibo Chen, Mingqian Liu, Yong Yang

item.title: Gorenstein and Ding injectivity over coherent rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.29347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a commutative Ding--Chen ring $B$, we prove that Gorenstein and Ding injectivity coincide over $R=B[x,y]/(x,y)^2$ if and only if injective $B$-modules generate the unbounded derived category of $B$. We construct a commutative von Neumann regular ring $B$ whose unbounded derived category is not generated by its pure injective objects. For this $B$, the coherent ring $R$ admits a strongly Gorenstein injective module $G$ which is not Ding injective. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module $G_{\mathfrak p}$ has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. The ring $R$ can be chosen to have cardinality $\aleph_\omega$, the least possible among coherent rings over which Gorenstein and Ding injectivity differ.
item.dc:creator: Guocheng Dai, Jiangsheng Hu

item.title: Admissible balanced pairs over cleft extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.29392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(B, A, i, e, l)$ be a cleft extension of abelian categories such that $e$ has a right adjoint $r$. It is proved that $(C, D)$ is an admissible balanced pair in $B$ if and only if $(\operatorname{add}(lC), \operatorname{add}(rD))$ is an admissible balanced pair in $A$. When the extension is directed with respect to a finite product decomposition of $B$, the lifting of complete hereditary cotorsion pairs $(C, Y)$ and $(X, D)$ to $A$ is characterized by the vanishing of first derived functors. Under a compatibility condition, the pair of special classes $(\Delta(C), \nabla(D))$ is then shown to be admissible balanced if and only if $(C, D)$ is. As an application, for rings $A, B$ and a $(B, A)$-bimodule $U$ of finite flat dimension over $A$ and finite projective dimension over $B$, the triangular matrix ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A & 0\\ U & B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is left virtually Gorenstein if and only if $A$ and $B$ are.
item.dc:creator: Junpeng Ren, Zheng-Gang Wu, Mengzhen Zhu

item.title: The axial radical
item.description: arXiv:2611.29405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An {\it axial algebra} is an algebra generated by a set $X$ of semisimple idempotents satisfying a prescribed set of fusion rules. Some axial algebras (such as primitive axial algebras of Jordan type $1/2$) have a Frobenius form, in which case one can define the radical $Rad(A)$ of the Frobenius form. Recently, Mamontov, S.~Shpectorov, and V.~Zhelyabin defined a radical $R(A;X)$ as the largest ideal not containing any axis of $X$, which is always contained in $Rad(A)$, and proved that $R(A;X) = Rad(A)$ when the Frobenius form is anisotropic. In this case they also proved that $A/R(A;X)$ is semisimple, yielding an elegant structure theory for primitive axial algebras with an anisotropic Frobenius form. Our objective is to recover these results, removing the assumption of a Frobenius form. We provide alternative characterizations of the radical, including a Jacobson-type radical (not the same as their Jacobson radical). We also replace the Frobenius form by a more general notion of orthogonality. Finally, we introduce a Baer-type radical and compare it to $R(A;X)$ and $Rad(A)$.
item.dc:creator: Louis Halle Rowen

item.title: The norm axiom and factor hyperfields
item.description: arXiv:2611.29473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Touchard and the author asked whether every valued hyperfield, in Krasner's sense with the norm axiom, is of the form $\mathcal{H}_\rho(K)$: a valued field $K$ read up to relative error $\rho$. The question turns on the norm axiom. If a valued hyperfield is a quotient $K^\times/T\cup\{0\}$ of a field, the norm axiom forces $T=1+\mathfrak{m}_\rho$ for a valuation on $K$. This completes the proof of a published proposition, and it makes the question equivalent to asking whether every Krasner valued hyperfield is such a quotient. For value group $\mathbb{Z}$ we prove directly that it is. Without the norm axiom the answer is negative. Layering a hyperfield over a non-trivial ordered abelian group gives a factor hyperfield exactly when the hyperfield itself is one, so Massouros's hyperfields yield hyperfields with a non-trivial valuation, satisfying all the other axioms, that are not factor hyperfields. The general question remains open.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Linzi

item.title: Higher Coherence of Flat Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.29508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish higher-coherence results for flat algebras over commutative base rings. If $K$ is noetherian and a $K$-flat algebra $A$ admits an $A^{\mathrm e}$-resolution of length $n$ with projective term in degree $n$ and flat terms in lower degrees, then every product of copies of $A$ has right flat dimension at most $n-1$ and $A$ is left strongly $n$-coherent. A projective $n$-th relative bar syzygy gives the corresponding two-sided conclusion. If $K$ is coherent and $A$ is $K$-flat and relatively quasi-free, then $A$ is left and right strongly $2$-coherent. In contrast, we construct a countable commutative ring $k$ that is strongly $n$-coherent for every $n\ge2$, while the one-variable polynomial algebra $k[z]$ is faithfully flat and relatively quasi-free over $k$ but fails strong $q$-coherence for every finite $q$. Explicit modules witness failure at each positive degree. These results establish coherence transfer over coherent bases and show that the analogous higher-degree transfer fails for every $n\ge2$, even after any fixed finite shift.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Pavlov, Mikhail Dusman

item.title: An example of a non-commutative division ring with abelian maximal subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.29601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a cyclic division algebra $D$ of degree $6$ with center $F$ algebraic over $\Q$. The multiplicative group $K^\times$ of a maximal subfield $K$ is maximal in $D^\times$, disproving Conjecture~C of Akbari, Ebrahimian, Momenaee Kermani, and Salehi Golsefidy. The field norm $N_{K/F}$ maps $K^\times$ onto $F^\times$, and its kernel is maximal in the reduced norm-one group $D^{(1)}$. The quotient $D^{(1)}/Z(D^{(1)})$ is nonabelian simple, with the image of $\ker N_{K/F}$ as an abelian maximal subgroup. The proof uses matrix factorizations over local fields, a convolution theorem of Breuillard and Glazer, and Moret--Bailly's theorem on points over extensions with prescribed splitting.
item.dc:creator: Huynh Viet Khanh

item.title: Gorenstein homological algebra over comma categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.29780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be abelian categories with enough projective objects. In this paper, we characterize those functors $F:\mathcal{A}\to \mathcal{B}$ for which the Gorenstein projective objects in the comma category $(F\downarrow \mathcal{B})$ admit an explicit description in terms of the Gorenstein projective objects of $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$. As a main application, we obtain estimates for the global Gorenstein projective dimension of $(F\downarrow \mathcal{B})$ in terms of those of $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ and the functor $F$, and derive exact formulas in several important cases. Our categorical approach also yields dual results concerning Gorenstein injective objects and dimension. Special attention is devoted to the module category over a triangular matrix ring $ \begin{pmatrix} A & 0\\ U & B \end{pmatrix}$, the product category $\mathcal{A}\times\mathcal{B}$, and the $n$-morphism category $Mor_n(\mathcal{C})$ associated with an abelian category $\mathcal{C}$ and an integer $n\geq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Rachid El Maaouy, J. R. Garc\'ia Rozas, Luis Oyonarte

item.title: Division rings of fractions of LV-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.29959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a field and let $A=L_K(E,\omega)$ be an LV-algebra of a row-finite weighted graph. We prove that $A$ embeds in a division ring if and only if $E$ has one vertex and its ordered loop weights satisfy $w_n=n$ and $w_j>j$ for $1\le j<n$. Under these conditions, $A$ has a universal division ring of fractions, which we identify with the free field on $2\sum_{j=1}^n w_j-n^2$ generators over $K$. We construct a free generating set explicitly by factoring the matrix of generators. We classify the resulting division rings over $K$ and bound the stabilization required to recognize invertible matrices. These results include mixed weights, for which the LV-algebra need not be a semifir.
item.dc:creator: Huynh Viet Khanh, Vo Hoang Thanh

item.title: The Fourth-Power Formula for the Antipode in AS-Gorenstein Hopf Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.30340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, for which homological integrals are defined, form a broad class of (infinite-dimensional) Hopf algebras. We establish an $S^4$ formula for left AS-Gorenstein Hopf algebras, thereby generalizing Radford's $S^4$ formula for finite-dimensional Hopf algebras and refining the formula of Brown and Zhang by identifying a group-like conjugating element in the Hopf algebra $H$. Our approach is to endow the space of left homological integrals $\int^{\ell}_H$ with a canonical right $H^*$-module structure compatible with its natural right $H$-action. If the $H^*$-action is rational, then $\int^{\ell}_H$ carries a canonical $(\mathrm{id}_H,S^4)$-twisted right-left Yetter--Drinfeld module structure. The right $H$-action and left $H$-coaction on this one-dimensional space determine a character and a group-like element in $H$, respectively; the twisted Yetter--Drinfeld compatibility condition then yields the $S^4$ formula. The $H^*$-action on $\int^{\ell}_H$ is rational if either the coradical of $H$ is coreflexive or the trivial left module $\Bbbk$ admits a finitely generated projective resolution. In particular, the latter condition holds when $H$ is left noetherian. We also establish a corresponding result for right AS-co-Gorenstein Hopf algebras with coreflexive coradical. As applications, we use the $S^4$ formula to study the bijectivity of the antipode and derive explicit finite-order bounds when $H$ is module-finite and faithfully flat over a central right coideal subalgebra, or finitely cogenerated and faithfully coflat over a cocentral quotient.
item.dc:creator: Quanshui Wu, Ruipeng Zhu

item.title: Weighted Numerical Homological Regularities over Positively Graded Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.30476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let A be a noetherian positively graded algebra. We investigate several weighted numerical homological regularities: weighted CM-regularity, weighted Tor-regularity (Ext-regularity), and weighted Ex-regularity, defined in terms of the weighted supremum or infimum degrees of canonical complexes associated with graded A-modules. Introduced by Kirkman, Won, and Zhang, weighted regularities provide finite invariants even when their unweighted counterparts are infinite. Through parametrized degree reweightings, they unify classical homological invariants, including unweighted numerical regularities, sup, inf, depth, projective dimension, and local cohomology dimension. This framework clarifies the behavior of homological regularities under degree shifts and reveals intrinsic relationships among these invariants, particularly those involving the a-invariant. We establish several inequalities and equalities relating these weighted regularities to the weighted supremum or infimum degrees of derived Hom and derived tensor complexes. These results recover their unweighted counterparts and yield new relations involving the a-invariant for a fixed weight. Some of these results generalize the inequalities of Kirkman-Won-Zhang between weighted CM-regularity and Tor-regularity by allowing the weight to range over the entire plane R^2. We also give conditions under which these inequalities become equalities, thereby answering a question posed by Kirkman-Won-Zhang. We use weighted AS-regularity to study the Artin-Schelter regularity of A. Under mild conditions, we prove that the weighted AS-regularity of A vanishes if and only if A is an N-graded AS-regular algebra. This generalizes an unweighted result of the present authors and a weighted result of Kirkman, Won, and Zhang.
item.dc:creator: Quanshui Wu, Bojuan Yi

item.title: Principal angles between annihilators of real sedenion zero divisors
item.description: arXiv:2611.30652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the relative geometry of annihilators of zero divisors in the real sedenion algebra. Each nonzero zero divisor has a four-dimensional annihilator, whose geometry is associated with an axis in the imaginary octonions. For two prescribed axes separated by an angle $\theta$, we establish the exact range of principal angles between their annihilators. The four principal cosines are necessarily $(p,p,q,q)$, where $\cos^2(\theta/2)\leq p\leq\cos(\theta/2)$ and $0\leq q\leq p$, and every admissible pair is realizable. We further derive an explicit quadratic formula for the principal cosines of any specified pair using two invariants of the associated quaternionic frames. A continuous deformation demonstrates that neither the axis angle nor the underlying quaternion subalgebras together determine the annihilator angles. Finally, we relate these results to the least singular subspaces of sedenion left multiplication through Euclidean projection onto the zero-divisor cone.
item.dc:creator: Shoot Koebisu

item.title: A symmetric eigenvalue lower bound for Hadamard products
item.description: arXiv:2611.30893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a positive semidefinite matrix $X$, let $\mu_k(X)$ be the minimum of the least eigenvalues of its principal submatrices of order $k$. For positive semidefinite $A,B$ of order $n$, we prove \[ \mu_{i+j-1}(A\circ B)\geq\mu_i(A)\mu_j(B), \qquad i,j\in\{1,2,\dots,n\},\quad i+j-1\leq n, \] and characterize equality when the right-hand side is positive. The resulting symmetric least-eigenvalue bound \[ \lambda_{\min}(A\circ B)\geq \max_{1\leq i\leq n}\mu_i(A)\mu_{n-i+1}(B) \] recovers the classical Schur lower bounds at endpoint choices and can be exact even when both factors are singular. It is incomparable with the projection bound from a recent companion paper, and combining the two bounds can improve on both. The proof combines a spectral minorant of $B$ whose diagonal entries are at least $\mu_j(B)$ with the projection inequality underlying the companion bound. Multifactor and Khatri--Rao consequences are also given.
item.dc:creator: Shengxuan Luo, Zai Yang

item.title: Quantales Arising From Rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.31109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the quantale, or multiplicative lattice, of additive submonoids of an arbitrary ring, with particular focus on the question of which properties of the ring can be recovered from it. We show that this quantale, unlike the better-known quantale of ideals, captures significant information about the cardinality, characteristic, and center of the ring. Certain rings, such as non-prime finite fields, torsion-free rings, and those with characteristic 2, are completely determined by their submonoid quantales. We also discuss various other subobject quantales one can associate to a (semi)ring.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Mesyan

item.title: Some attractive bases for the Onsager Lie algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.28581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Onsager Lie algebra $\mathcal{O}$ is defined by generators $A$, $B$ subject to the Dolan-Grady relations $[A,[A,[A,B]]] = 4[A,B]$ and $[B,[B,[B,A]]] = 4[B,A]$. It is known that $\mathcal{O}$ is infinite-dimensional. In this paper, we consider three bases for $\mathcal{O}$. The first basis was recently introduced by the author, and the second basis is a variation of the first. The third basis was introduced by Baseilhac and Cramp\'e in 2019. By construction, the elements in each basis are recursively obtained from $A$, $B$. Using the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ loop algebra, we express every basis element in closed form. We then describe how these three bases are related to each other. Next, we consider a finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-module $V$. Associated with $V$ are six well-known decompositions: the eigenspace decomposition of $A$ and the eigenspace decomposition of $B$, together with four other decompositions of $V$ said to be split. We show that on each decomposition, every element of the first two bases acts in a block diagonal, block upper bidiagonal, block lower bidiagonal, or block tridiagonal fashion. We illustrate these actions using a tetrahedron diagram. We also determine how the elements of the third basis act on the six decompositions. To obtain our results about finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathcal{O}$-modules, we use the theory of tridiagonal pairs.
item.dc:creator: Jae-Ho Lee

item.title: Lagrangian Construction of the Enveloping Superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$
item.description: arXiv:2611.28832v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a Lagrangian construction of the enveloping superalgebra $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$. More precisely, we realize the Schur superalgebra $S(m|n,r)$, the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n})$ on $(\mathbb Q^{m|n})^{\otimes r}$, via the top Borel--Moore homology of mixed Steinberg varieties. Their top-dimensional components are indexed by the admissible matrices of Du and Rui and meet a natural symplectic open subset in Lagrangian subvarieties. As applications, we realize the irreducible polynomial representations of $\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n}$ on the relevant homology of the fibers of these maps, establish a geometric $(\mathfrak{gl}_{m|n},\mathfrak{gl}_{k|l})$-Howe duality and confirm new cases of a conjecture of Douglass and R\"ohrle on generalized Steinberg varieties.
item.dc:creator: Yang Yang

item.title: $\mathcal{PGF}=\mathcal{GP}$ over commutative Noetherian rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.28900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove $\mathcal{PGF}=\mathcal{GP}$ over every commutative Noetherian ring.
item.dc:creator: Yuhui Hua, Shun-Jie Li, Chencheng Zhang

item.title: Strong holonomicity of functions on curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.29063v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth affine irreducible curve over $\mathbb C$, and let ${\mathcal D} = {\mathcal D} (X)$ be the ring of global differential operators on $X$. To every nonzero operator $L \in {\mathcal D} $ we attach a non-negative integer $n(L)$, the holonomicity index of $L$, which is defined in an elementary way, by counting solutions of $L$ in the truncated local rings at the singular points of $L$. Our main theorem shows that $n(L)$ coincides with the Calogero--Moser index of the Weyl closure ${\rm cl}(L) = {\mathcal D}(K) \cap {\mathcal D} $ of $L$, i.e. with the integer $n$ labelling the Calogero--Moser space $ {\mathcal C}_n(X,\mathcal{I})$ that contains the isomorphism class of the left ideal ${\rm cl}(L)$ under the classification of ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ given in [Berest--Chalykh, 2012]. The proof is based on a dual version of the Cannings--Holland correspondence, which describes left ideals of ${\mathcal D}$ in terms of finite-dimensional spaces of algebraic distributions on $X$, and an explicit formula for the Calogero--Moser index given in terms of these distributions. We apply these results to annihilators of locally holomorphic functions on $X$: we call a holonomic function $f$ strongly holonomic if the Calogero--Moser index of ${\rm Ann}_{\mathcal D}(f)$ is positive, and we compute this index in a number of interesting cases.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Berest, Isaac Goldberg

item.title: A Determinant Proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.29308v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an elementary proof of the determinant identity in \cite[Conjecture~A.1]{SYZ} over any field of odd characteristic $p$. The proof computes the determinant of a single linear map by dividing by two different monic polynomials. By \cite[Proposition~A.9]{SYZ}, the identity gives another proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo conjecture. The conjecture identifies the Higgs--de Rham self-map of the four-pointed projective line with the map induced by multiplication by $p$ on its elliptic double cover.
item.dc:creator: Jinbang Yang

item.title: The Kaplansky-Aupetit conjecture for C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.29761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We settle the Kaplansky--Aupetit conjecture when either algebra is a $C^*$-algebra. More precisely, if $A$ is a unital Banach algebra and $B$ is a unital $C^*$-algebra, or if $A$ is a unital $C^*$-algebra and $B$ is a unital semisimple Banach algebra, then every unital invertibility-preserving linear surjection $\phi: A\to B$ is a Jordan homomorphism. In fact, it suffices to assume that $\phi$ preserves the invertibility of products of two exponentials, or of individual exponentials when both algebras are $C^*$-algebras. Claude Opus 5.5 found the original proof when both $A$ and $B$ are $C^*$-algebras by adapting a resolvent estimate from a recent preprint of Colbrook and Stepaniants, while OpenAI's GPT-6.1 further generalized this to the case where only one algebra is a $C^*$-algebra.
item.dc:creator: Ilja Gogi\'{c}, Bojan Kuzma

item.title: Endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules in special characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2611.30299v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the division algebras that occur as endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules of a given rank in special characteristic which cannot be defined over a finite field. The classification is in terms of the center of the algebra and its local invariants. Together with the known results in generic characteristic and over finite fields, this gives a complete description of the endomorphism algebras of Drinfeld modules of a given rank.
item.dc:creator: Mihran Papikian

item.title: Involutions in the Cayley-Dickson construction
item.description: arXiv:2606.27798v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine all involutions in the Cayley-Dickson construction that extend the involution of the original $*$-algebra. We also find all algebra isomorphisms between the resulting Cayley doubles that extend the identity automorphism of the original $*$-algebra, and consequently classify the resulting $*$-algebras up to such $*$-algebra isomorphisms. As applications, we show that Cayley doubles of algebras without zero divisors admit exactly one additional extension of the original involution in the 2-torsion-free case and none otherwise, prove that the classical Cayley-Dickson involution is the unique scalar involution, and obtain a classification of the $*$-algebras arising from $\mathbb{R}$ up to dimension 4.
item.dc:creator: Masood Aryapoor, Per B\"ack, Sophie Pautrel

item.title: A note on some upper bounds for the Frobenius norm of the $q$-deformed commutator
item.description: arXiv:2608.03897v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For two square complex matrices $A,B,$ and a real number $q$, the $q$-deformed commutator of $A$ and $B$ is defined as $AB-qBA$. We give some upper bounds on the Frobenius norm of the $q$-deformed commutator in the case $q\ge0$. All of the inequalities derived in this paper generalize the B\"{o}ttcher-Wenzel inequality.
item.dc:creator: Motoyuki Nobori

item.title: Entrywise Positivity Preservers on Green Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2608.18491v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify entrywise functions preserving positive semidefiniteness on Green matrices with positive parameters. For each fixed \(n\ge2\), PSD preservation is equivalent to \(f\) being nondecreasing and \((f(tr^{i+j}))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) being PSD for all \(t>0,r>1\). For \(f\in C^{2n-2}\), this is equivalent to \(f'\ge0\) and positive semidefiniteness of \(((t\,d/dt)^{i+j}f(t))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) at every positive \(t\). These fixed-order classes strictly decrease with \(n\); their intersection consists exactly of \(f(t)=\int_{[0,\infty)}t^\alpha\,d\mu(\alpha)\), where \(\mu\) is a finite positive measure and the integral is finite for every \(t>0\). At each fixed order, entrywise Loewner monotonicity is equivalent to \(f\in C^1\) and \(f'\) belonging to the corresponding PSD preserver class. In all orders, monotonicity itself implies smoothness. Nonnegative minors of orders one and two on every strict three-by-three Green input already force \(f\equiv0\) or \(f(t)=ct^\alpha\), with \(c>0\) and \(\alpha\ge0\). They give TN output in every order; the nonzero members also preserve PSD Green structure. We also classify PSD, TN, and Loewner-monotone extensions to the closure allowing zero entries. No regularity is assumed except in the differential criterion.
item.dc:creator: Wei Xie

item.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
item.description: arXiv:2609.11588v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm that computes multiplication in $A_n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2\in R^\times$ using $O(N\log N)$ arithmetic operations and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage, given $A_n$ is defined with doubling parameters that are units with square roots in a fixed commutative algebra finitely generated as an $R$-module admitting a linear surjection onto the base ring preserving the identity. These conditions are satisfied by every Cayley-Dickson tower over $\mathbb{R}$ and over finite fields of odd characteristic, where the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ is at most $(36n-69)2^{n-3}+10$ for $n\ge4$. To the author's knowledge, this is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. In single-core benchmarks over $\mathbb{R}$, an open-source implementation in the library fastCD is approximately $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Lemley

item.title: Generalized Commutator on Octonion Algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.04466v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be an octonion algebra over a field $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and let $A,B\in\mathcal O$, not both zero. We study the image of the generalized commutator $\Phi(x,y)=A(xy)-B(yx)$ on $\mathcal O$. We prove that $\Phi$ is surjective if and only if either one of $A$ and $B$ is invertible and $A\neq B$, or $A$ and $B$ are nonzero zero divisors and $A-B$ is invertible. In the remaining cases, the image of $\Phi$ is a hyperplane or a four-dimensional maximal totally isotropic subspace of $\mathcal O$, except when $A$ and $B$ are linearly independent zero divisors and $A-B$ is not invertible, in which case the image spans a six-dimensional subspace. Along the way, we show that every octonion of trace zero is a commutator. We also prove that the image of $Axy-Byx$ on any quaternion algebra over $F$ is a vector subspace, extending a result of Panja S., Saini P. and Singh A. (Images of polynomial maps with constants, Mathematika 71 (2025), no. 3, Paper No. e70031) for $2\times 2$ matrices over algebraically closed fields, and we give examples of other generalized polynomials whose images are not vector subspaces.
item.dc:creator: Thiago Castilho De Mello, Prachi Saini

item.title: A Cubic Obstruction to Sums of Tripotent and Square-Zero Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.24594v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring of characteristic $2$, and let $\lambda$ be a central unit of $R$. We prove that an element $a\in R$ satisfying $a^3+a^2+\lambda=0$ cannot be expressed as the sum of a tripotent element and a square-zero element. The proof does not require the summands to commute. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$, this gives counterexamples in every order divisible by three, including order twelve, and proves the optimality of the known uniform exponent four in those orders. We also give constructive proofs that every matrix of order four or five over $\mathbb{F}_2$ is a sum of a tripotent and a square-zero matrix, and deduce a complete criterion in order three. Combining the cubic obstruction with the quartic obstruction for idempotent-plus-cube-zero decompositions, we obtain two-way incomparability of the corresponding decomposition classes in every positive order divisible by twelve.
item.dc:creator: Dang Vo Phuc, Peter V. Danchev

item.title: Topological Frobenius algebras
item.description: arXiv:2209.02979v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define in a graded and topologized setting the notions of unital/counital/biunital infinitesimal anti-symmetric bialgebras and coFrobenius bialgebras and discuss their algebraic properties. We also define in this setting the notion of a 2D open-closed TQFT. We illustrate these structures with old and new examples of geometric origin that arise in contexts as varied as symplectic topology, string topology, manifold topology, and quantum homology. The underlying vector spaces, which are typically infinite dimensional, belong to a class of topological vector spaces known as Tate vector spaces.
item.dc:creator: Kai Cieliebak, Alexandru Oancea

item.title: An upper bound for the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of relative Sullivan algebras
item.description: arXiv:2404.18939v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper addresses a question posed by F\'elix, Halperin and Thomas. We prove that the Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of a relative Sullivan algebra is finite if such invariants of the base algebra and fiber algebra are both finite. Furthermore, we provide a similar estimation for the Toomer invariant.
item.dc:creator: Jiawei Zhou

item.title: New codes from algebras of direct products of groups
item.description: arXiv:2412.09695v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper deals with the algebraic-combinatorial description of group codes by using the Wedderburn-Artin decomposition of semisimple group algebras. Concretely, we give a detailed description of the Wedderburn-Artin decomposition of the semisimple group algebra associated with a direct product of finite groups that are cyclic, dihedral, or generalised quaternion. This, in turn, provides a group-algebraic framework for computing all linear codes generated by such groups. As a consequence, we find new linear codes that improve the best-known minimum distance for their length and dimension. We conclude the paper by discussing how group codes arised from some explicit Wedderburn-Artin decomposition can be utilised to construct quantum codes in a systematic way.
item.dc:creator: Markus Grassl, Miguel Sales-Cabrera, Xaro Soler-Escriv\`a, V\'ictor Sotomayor

item.title: Primitivity Testing in Free Group Algebras via Duality
item.description: arXiv:2502.12885v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a free group. By a classical result of Cohn and Lewin, the free group algebra $K\left[F\right]$ is a free ideal ring (FIR): a ring over which the submodules of free modules are themselves free, and of a well-defined rank. Given a finitely generated right ideal $I\leq K\left[F\right]$ and an element $f\in I$, we give an explicit algorithm determining whether $f$ is part of some basis of $I$. More generally, given free $K[F]$-modules $M\le N$, we provide algorithms determining whether $M$ is a free summand of $N$, and whether $N$ admits a free splitting relative to $M$. These can also be used to obtain analogous algorithms for free groups $H\le J$. As an aside, we also provide an algorithm to compute the intersection of two given submodules of a free $K\left[F\right]$-module. A key feature of this work is the introduction of a duality, induced by a matrix with entries in a free ideal ring, between the respective algebraic extensions of its column and row spaces.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: J. London Math. Soc. 113 (2026), no. 6, e70599
item.dc:creator: Matan Seidel, Danielle Ernst-West, Doron Puder

item.title: Kapranov $L_{\infty}[1]$ algebras
item.description: arXiv:2509.26341v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given any K\"ahler manifold $X$, Kapranov discovered a nontrivial $L_\infty[1]$ algebra structure on $\Omega^{0,\bullet}_{X}(T^{1,0}X)$. Motivated by this result, we introduce the notion of an $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra, generalizing $L_\infty[1]$ algebras, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is a differential graded commutative algebra with unit. We extend standard notions such as quasi-isomorphism and linearization to this setting and establish a linearization theorem. As an application, we prove that any DG Lie algebroid $(\mathcal{L},Q_{\mathcal{L}})$ over a DG manifold $(\mathcal{M},Q)$ induces a distinguished isomorphism class of $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures on $\Gamma(\mathcal{L})$, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is the DG commutative algebra $(C^\infty(\mathcal{M}),Q)$. Their unary bracket is $Q_{\mathcal{L}}$, while their binary bracket is a cocycle representative of the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid. All these isomorphic $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures are $\mathfrak{R}$-linearizable if and only if the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid vanishes. In contrast, the induced $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathbb{K}$-algebra structures on $\Gamma(\mathcal{L})$ are necessarily $\mathbb{K}$-linearizable, hence $\mathbb{K}$-homotopy abelian.
item.dc:creator: Ruggero Bandiera, Seokbong Seol, Mathieu Sti\'enon, Ping Xu

item.title: Extracting Exact Lie Derivatives Without Backpropagation: A Dual Compiler for Neural Control Barrier Functions
item.description: arXiv:2604.23995v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A safety filter based on a neural control barrier function (CBF) evaluates, at each control cycle, the trained network and its Lie derivatives along the system vector fields. This paper presents a compiler whose emitted C++ code performs this evaluation on embedded processors by forward-mode differentiation with dual numbers. The derivatives are exact in the sense of automatic differentiation, which means that they are free of truncation error and subject to floating-point roundoff. One evaluation of the network in this arithmetic, called a dual pass, returns the barrier value and its Lie derivative along one vector field, and an extension to hyper-dual numbers returns the second-order Lie derivatives of CBFs of relative degree two. Apart from scalar variables, the memory that a dual pass writes is at most four floating-point numbers per neuron of the widest layer and does not depend on the network depth. On an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, we compare the emitted code with code for reverse-mode differentiation (i.e., backpropagation), which is also generated before the program runs and uses fixed-size arrays. In three experiments, the reverse-mode code has a lower execution time than the dual and hyper-dual passes executed one after the other. For single-input networks, the measurements do not establish such an ordering between the reverse-mode code and a variant of the dual pass that propagates the real part once. For networks of increasing depth, the working memory of the dual passes is constant, whereas that of the reverse-mode code increases. While the emitted code runs, no dynamic allocation is recorded. We report the maximum observed execution time of the complete filter step, which includes the dynamics and a breakpoint search for the quadratic program with input bounds and one affine constraint. The compiler and the experiments are open source.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Kamaldar

item.title: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
item.description: arXiv:2608.30740v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules. For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture. Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Tomonaga

item.title: Direct products of Gorenstein flat modules over coherent rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.22078v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a commutative coherent local algebra of Krull dimension zero and a countably generated projectively coresolved Gorenstein flat module whose countable power has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. This answers negatively the question of whether Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring are closed under direct products. As a consequence, we obtain a pure-injective Ding injective module whose character module has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension and whose character bidual has infinite Gorenstein injective dimension. We also give equivalent conditions for Gorenstein flat modules over a right coherent ring to be closed under direct products, in terms of relative Mittag--Leffler conditions, stationarity, and Gorenstein flat and injective dimensions of character biduals. For the constructed ring, we exhibit a decreasing countable sequence of strong submodules of a free module whose intersection has infinite Gorenstein flat dimension. Thus the abstract elementary class of Gorenstein flat modules, with the strong submodule relation, has finite character but does not admit intersections.
item.dc:creator: Guocheng Dai, Jiangsheng Hu

item.title: Enumerating Solutions to Type (2,3) Composition Identities of Finite Endofunctions
item.description: arXiv:2611.19668v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We enumerate ordered pairs $(f,g)$ of endofunctions on a finite labeled set $X$ satisfying a composition identity of type $(2,3)$, with two factors on one side and three on the other. For all sixteen forms up to exchanging $f$ and $g$, we give exact counting formulas as functions of $|X|$ in terms of finite sums and generating functions. Such pairs correspond bijectively to actions on $X$ of the semigroup presented by two generators and the prescribed relation. The proofs use images, fibers, and the decomposition of functional digraphs into directed cycles with rooted trees attached. Several constructions apply beyond these sixteen identities: they give recurrences for homomorphisms between arbitrary prescribed functional digraphs and formulas for pairs satisfying $f^a=g^b$, where $a,b$ are fixed positive integers. We also derive an explicit inclusion-exclusion formula over subsets of $X$ for the number of endofunctions $g$ on $X$ satisfying $B=gAg$ for arbitrary prescribed endofunctions $A,B$ on $X$. This generalizes the enumeration of compositional square roots, recovered when $A$ is the identity map.
item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev
